_meta.title: Financial structures evaluated for the DFCC GCF pipeline
_meta.source: DFCC DAE Readiness Pre-Qualified Delivery Partner ToR, version 21 November 2025, Lot 2 — which asks for five to seven innovative instruments to be evaluated and their viability shown with and without concessional support.
_meta.note: Each structure is scored against what DFCC is actually accredited to deliver. The grant modality is NOT ticked in DFCC's accreditation, so a structure that needs it is marked not deliverable by DFCC as the accredited entity — a finding to verify with DFCC or the NDA, not a judgement on the structure.
_meta.concessionalityNote: GCF applies minimum concessionality: no more concession than is needed to make the project viable. A structure that delivers the same outcome with less subsidy is preferred, which is why grant-equivalent is scored and not just headline size.

barriers.label: No long-tenor debt available
barriers.detail: Local bank tenors are shorter than the asset life, so the project cannot be financed at a tariff it can support.

barriers.label: Offtake or counterparty credit risk
barriers.detail: The revenue counterparty is not investment grade or has no track record on this contract type.

barriers.label: Currency mismatch
barriers.detail: Costs or debt in USD against revenue in LKR, with no affordable hedge at the tenor required.

barriers.label: First-of-kind locally
barriers.detail: The technology is proven elsewhere but has no local operating record, so lenders price risk they cannot yet measure.

barriers.label: Upfront capital against deferred savings
barriers.detail: Benefits accrue over years as avoided cost; the capital is needed now and the payback exceeds available tenor.

barriers.label: Outcome is not monetised
barriers.detail: The result is a public good — resilience, ecosystem services — with no cash flow to service debt.

barriers.label: Many small borrowers
barriers.detail: Transaction cost per borrower exceeds what a commercial lender can recover at the ticket size involved.

instruments.name: Concessional on-lent credit line
instruments.summary: GCF provides a long-tenor concessional facility that DFCC on-lends. Concession is bought as tenor and grace, not as margin.
instruments.mobilisationNote: Each GCF dollar sits alongside DFCC and sponsor equity at the project level.
instruments.dfccRole: Lender of record, credit risk retained by DFCC.
instruments.watchOut: Does nothing for a project whose problem is counterparty risk rather than tenor.

instruments.name: Partial credit guarantee / first-loss risk sharing
instruments.summary: GCF funds a first-loss or pari-passu guarantee tranche so DFCC can lend against risk it would otherwise decline.
instruments.mobilisationNote: A guarantee mobilises a multiple of its own size, so the leverage per GCF dollar is the highest of the seven.
instruments.dfccRole: Originates and services; GCF carries a defined slice of loss.
instruments.watchOut: Priced wrong it subsidises lending that would have happened anyway — the clearest place minimum concessionality bites.

instruments.name: Blended sustainability-linked loan
instruments.summary: Commercial and concessional tranches blended into one facility, with a margin ratchet on verified KPIs.
instruments.mobilisationNote: The commercial tranche is mobilised directly by the concessional one.
instruments.dfccRole: Arranger and lender; KPI verification is DFCC's monitoring obligation.
instruments.watchOut: The ratchet is only as good as the KPI. A KPI the borrower was going to hit anyway is a discount, not an incentive.

instruments.name: Subordinated / mezzanine tranche
instruments.summary: GCF takes a junior position so senior commercial debt sees an acceptable risk profile.
instruments.mobilisationNote: Senior lenders are crowded in behind the junior tranche.
instruments.dfccRole: Senior lender alongside; may also arrange.
instruments.watchOut: Junior capital is where losses land first; the appraisal has to be honest about the downside case.

instruments.name: Results-based payment on verified outcomes
instruments.summary: Payment released against independently verified results rather than against expenditure.
instruments.mobilisationNote: Mobilises against a future payment, so it needs a party able to pre-finance.
instruments.dfccRole: Not deliverable by DFCC as the accredited entity — a results-based payment is a grant instrument and DFCC's accreditation does not carry the grant modality.
instruments.watchOut: The only structure here that reaches a project with no cash flow, and the one DFCC currently cannot deliver. That combination is the pipeline's structural gap.

instruments.name: Warehouse and refinance through a green bond
instruments.summary: DFCC warehouses eligible loans, then refinances the portfolio through a labelled bond, recycling capacity.
instruments.mobilisationNote: Capital recycles: the same balance sheet writes the next cohort.
instruments.dfccRole: Originator and issuer; requires a taxonomy-aligned eligibility register.
instruments.watchOut: Needs a domestic bond market with appetite at the tenor. Depends on sovereign conditions outside the project's control.

instruments.name: Local-currency lending / FX risk facility
instruments.summary: GCF absorbs or prices the currency mismatch so the borrower services debt in the currency it earns.
instruments.mobilisationNote: Unlocks lending rather than co-investing alongside it.
instruments.dfccRole: Lends in LKR against a USD facility with the mismatch covered.
instruments.watchOut: Currency risk is not removed by being moved. Whoever holds it must be able to carry it.
